title: Consistency of a mixed layer depth operator with each model's own mlotst output
window: 1971-01 to 2000-12, the March and September climatologies

method.criterion: potential density threshold 0.03 kg/m3, referenced to each model's shallowest level, crossing depth interpolated between the bracketing levels
method.order_of_operations: MLD computed for each of the 30 months, then averaged; the profiles are never averaged first
method.climatology_rule: a cell enters either climatology only if all 30 years are valid there
method.grid: every number on the model's native grid, weighted by its own areacello; no regridding except the display maps in figure 1

consistency_ranking_criterion: mean RMSD over March and September, smallest first

threshold_sensitivity.note: operator against the same month's mlotst at the protocol's 0.03 kg/m3 and at the larger 0.125 kg/m3; not part of the graded answer

method_notes: The MLD is computed month by month and averaged afterwards. One MLD taken from the 30-year mean profiles would be systematically shallower and is the main error to avoid.
The reference depth is each model's shallowest level, because all three publish mlotst as sigma-T referenced to the ocean surface, not to 10 m.

The density threshold is 0.03 kg/m3, the value the CMIP6 protocol defines mlotst with: a buoyancy difference of 0.0003 m s-2, which Griffies et al. (2016, H24) equate to 0.03 kg/m3 and attribute to Levitus (1982). At the larger 0.125 kg/m3 some studies use, the 1971-03 RMSD against mlotst rises from CESM2 18 to 86 m, GFDL-ESM4 39 to 90 m, MPI-ESM1-2-LR 23 to 60 m.
Area percentages are fractions of ocean AREA, weighted by each model's areacello, not fractions of grid cells; on a curvilinear grid the two differ substantially.

Cells where the threshold is never reached leave the operator MLD undefined; they are excluded from both climatologies and from the denominator, and the shared-area percentage records how much was dropped. Excluding them is necessary, not only convenient: the models' own mlotst encodes such columns differently (GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR report roughly the full column depth, CESM2 mostly 0 m), so no single fill value is fair to all three.
why_they_differ: Both fields come from the same simulation, so the residual is a property of the two diagnostics. The protocol computes mlotst online at every time step, from a surface parcel moved to each level's own pressure, and archives the monthly mean of those instantaneous depths (Griffies et al. 2016, H24). The operator takes a sigma0 difference on the monthly-mean profile. A monthly mean is itself an averaged profile, so the smoothing that makes a 30-year-mean profile too shallow also makes the monthly one shallower than the mean of the instantaneous depths: the bias is expected to be negative, and it is negative in 6 of the 6 model-and-month combinations.

GFDL-ESM4 computes mlotst on its native 75 hybrid layers with a 2 m top layer, but its archived thetao and so were remapped to 35 z levels and regridded to 1 degree, so the operator sees a coarser profile than the model's own diagnostic did. Part of its larger RMSD is therefore the archive's resolution, and the ranking measures consistency between the archived fields, not the quality of the model's mixed layer.
